The core fix is correct and well-reasoned. The old code captured writeBus/writeAddr from globals after a D-Bus yield point,, where interleaving coroutines could corrupt them.

The new code snapshots bus/addr from deviceHashes before the yield and stores them in a per-device FruWriteCtx — this eliminates the race entirely.

One minor gap: writeTimerDevId is still a single global. If two devices have in-progress partial writes (neither has reached atEnd), the second device overwrites writeTimerDevId, and the first device's buffered data is never flushed by the timer.

please correct me if my understanding is wrong ?

Thanks. Your understanding is correct. The single writeTimerDevId global cannot track multiple in-progress partial writes. In the updated patch (Patch Set 4), I moved the timer into FruWriteCtx so each devId has its own independent timer.

writeTimerDevId is a single variable but fruWriteCtxMap supports multiple devices. If two devices have partial writes pending, the second one overwrites writeTimerDevId, and the first device's data is never flushed.

Should this be a per-device timer inside FruWriteCtx?
Yes, agreed. Patch Set 4 moves the timer into FruWriteCtx. Each device now owns its timer.
Only one device gets flushed when the timer fires. Other entries in fruWriteCtxMap with active=true remain stuck forever.
Thanks. I pushed the patch set 4 to fix the design gap.
This unconditionally overwrites any previously stored devId. If another device had a pending timer flush, it's silently dropped.
Thanks. I pushed the patch set 4 to fix the design gap.

These lg2::info calls will log on every FRU write segment and every timer flush. On systems with frequent FRU writes (e.g., SPD data updates, multi-device provisioning), this could flood the journal.

Should these be lg2::debug instead? lg2::info is typically reserved for infrequent, operationally significant events. The debug level would still be available when needed via busctl set-property to raise the log level.
Thanks, Agree. These were added for root cause verification during development. I changed them to lg2::debug.

FRU image data and timer remain allocated after write completes. Please erase the map entry to avoid unbounded memory growth in this long-running daemon

I further made a small modification: Entries are erased from fruWriteCtxMap on atEnd completion. Timer callback paths release only the data buffer because they execute inside sdbusplus::Timer::timeoutHandler(), which continues to access eventSource after the user callback returns.
operator[] inserts a default entry before validation. If deviceHashes.find() fails, an empty entry leaks. Please move the deviceHashes check first and use try_emplace after.
Thanks for your review. I reordered to find() first, validate fruDeviceId against deviceHashes, then try_emplace() only after all checks pass. Invalid IDs no longer mutate the map.
